\subsection*{Randomized --- Expected Time: Results}

\begin{definition}[Prefix stability]
\lean{Randomized.IsPrefixStable}
\label{Randomized.IsPrefixStable}
\leanok
A function $r$ from finite Boolean strings to optional values is prefix stable if,
whenever it returns a value $a$ on a string $w$, it returns that same value on every
extension formed by appending another finite Boolean string $v$ to $w$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[A halting prefix determines the full run]
\lean{Randomized.IsPrefixStable.of_take}
\label{Randomized.IsPrefixStable.of_take}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.IsPrefixStable}
\difficulty{1}
Let $r$ map bit strings to optional values, and suppose that once $r$ returns a value on
a string, it returns the same value on every extension of that string. For any bit
string $w$, natural number $t$, and value $a$, if $r$ returns $a$ on the prefix of $w$
of length $t$, then $r$ returns $a$ on $w$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[A prefix of a nonhalting run does not halt]
\lean{Randomized.IsPrefixStable.take_eq_none}
\label{Randomized.IsPrefixStable.take_eq_none}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.IsPrefixStable, Randomized.IsPrefixStable.of_take}
\difficulty{4}
Let $r$ map bit strings to optional values, and suppose that once $r$ returns a value on
a string, it returns the same value on every extension of that string. If $r$ returns no
value on a bit string $w$, then it returns no value on every prefix of $w$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Repeated run]
\lean{Randomized.repeatRun}
\label{Randomized.repeatRun}
\leanok
Given a function $q$ from finite Boolean strings to optional values, a natural number
$t$, and a finite Boolean string $w$, define the repeated run recursively as follows: if
$0<t\leq |w|$, take the first available value among the result of applying $q$ to the
length-$t$ prefix of $w$ and the repeated run of the remaining suffix; otherwise return
no value.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Recursive decomposition of repeated runs]
\lean{Randomized.repeatRun_of_le}
\label{Randomized.repeatRun_of_le}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.repeatRun}
\difficulty{1}
Let $q$ map finite bit strings to optional values in a type $\alpha$, and let $t$ be a
positive natural number. For every bit string $w$ whose length is at least $t$, the
repeated-run procedure returns the left-biased optional choice between applying $q$ to
the first $t$ bits of $w$ and running the procedure on the remaining suffix.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[No complete block means no result]
\lean{Randomized.repeatRun_of_lt}
\label{Randomized.repeatRun_of_lt}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.repeatRun}
\difficulty{2}
Let $q$ map finite bit strings to optional values in a type $\alpha$, and let $t$ be a
natural number. If a bit string $w$ has length less than $t$, then the repeated-run
procedure returns no value on $w$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Prefix stability of repeated runs]
\lean{Randomized.repeatRun_isPrefixStable}
\label{Randomized.repeatRun_isPrefixStable}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.IsPrefixStable, Randomized.repeatRun, Randomized.repeatRun_of_le}
\difficulty{6}
Let $\alpha$ be a type, let $q$ map finite bit strings to optional values in $\alpha$, and let
$t$ be a natural number. The procedure that examines successive blocks of length $t$ and
returns the first value of $q$ that is present is prefix-stable: if it returns a value
on a string $w$, then it returns the same value on every extension of $w$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[A Successful Repeated Run Has a Successful Block]
\lean{Randomized.exists_of_repeatRun_eq_some}
\label{Randomized.exists_of_repeatRun_eq_some}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.repeatRun, Randomized.repeatRun_of_le}
\difficulty{6}
Let $q$ map Boolean lists to optional values, let $t$ be a natural number, and let $w$
be a Boolean list. If the repeated run of $q$ on $w$ returns $a$, then there is a
Boolean list $u$ of length exactly $t$ on which $q$ returns $a$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Probability of not halting]
\lean{Randomized.notHaltedProb}
\label{Randomized.notHaltedProb}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.randProb}
For a function $r$ from finite Boolean strings to optional values and a natural number
$t$, the probability of not halting by time $t$ is the fraction of length-$t$ Boolean
strings $w$ for which $r(w)$ has no value, under the uniform distribution on those
strings.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Bounded cumulative nonhalting probability]
\lean{Randomized.ExpTimeLe}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch07-randomized-computation}{
  pdf-26d95080dbde-p006-b004,
  pdf-26d95080dbde-p010-b001
}
\label{Randomized.ExpTimeLe}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.notHaltedProb}
Let $r$ be a randomized procedure mapping finite Boolean strings to either an output in
$\alpha$ or no output, where $\alpha$ has decidable equality. Say that its nonhalting
probability at time $t$ is $p_t$. The sum of $p_t$ over the first $K$ time indices is at
most the rational number $B$, for every natural number $K$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Nonnegativity of nonhalting probability]
\lean{Randomized.notHaltedProb_nonneg}
\label{Randomized.notHaltedProb_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.notHaltedProb, Randomized.randProb_nonneg}
\difficulty{1}
For every natural number $t$ and every randomized procedure that returns either an
output or no output on a finite bit string, the probability that it returns no output on
a uniformly random string of $t$ bits is nonnegative.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bound on nonhalting probability]
\lean{Randomized.notHaltedProb_le_one}
\label{Randomized.notHaltedProb_le_one}
\leanok

\difficulty{1}
For every natural number $t$ and every randomized procedure that returns either an
output or no output on a finite bit string, the probability that it returns no output on
a uniformly random string of $t$ bits is at most $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of Nonhalting Probability]
\lean{Randomized.notHaltedProb_le_of_le}
\label{Randomized.notHaltedProb_le_of_le}
\leanok

\difficulty{3}
Let $\alpha$ be a type and let $r$ map bit strings to optional elements of $\alpha$. Suppose
halting is prefix stable: once $r(w)$ returns a value, it returns the same value on
every extension of $w$. For natural numbers $s\le t$, the probability that $r$ has not
halted on a uniformly random length-$t$ bit string is at most the corresponding
probability at length $s$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Nonnegativity of an expected-time bound]
\lean{Randomized.ExpTimeLe.nonneg}
\label{Randomized.ExpTimeLe.nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.ExpTimeLe}
\difficulty{1}
Let $\alpha$ be a type with decidable equality, let
$r\colon\{0,1\}^*\to\mathrm{Option}(\alpha)$, and let $B\in\mathbb{Q}$. If, for every
natural number $K$, the sum over $0\le t<K$ of the probability that $r$ has not halted
after $t$ random bits is at most $B$, then $B\ge 0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bound on Nonhalting Probability]
\lean{Randomized.mul_notHaltedProb_le}
\label{Randomized.mul_notHaltedProb_le}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.ExpTimeLe, Randomized.IsPrefixStable, Randomized.notHaltedProb, Randomized.notHaltedProb_le_of_le}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\alpha$ be a type, let $r$ map bit strings to optional elements of $\alpha$, and suppose
halting is prefix stable: once $r(w)$ returns a value, it returns the same value on
every extension of $w$. If there is a rational number $B$ such that for every natural
number $K$, the sum of the nonhalting probabilities of $r$ over times $0,\ldots,K-1$ is at
most $B$, then for every natural number $t$, $t$ times the probability that $r$ has not
halted on a uniformly random length-$t$ bit string is at most $B$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Nonhalting Probability Bound at Positive Time]
\lean{Randomized.notHaltedProb_le_div}
\label{Randomized.notHaltedProb_le_div}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.ExpTimeLe, Randomized.IsPrefixStable, Randomized.mul_notHaltedProb_le, Randomized.notHaltedProb}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\alpha$ be a type, let $r$ map bit strings to optional elements of $\alpha$, and suppose
halting is prefix stable: once $r(w)$ returns a value, it returns the same value on
every extension of $w$. If, for some rational number $B$, the sum of the nonhalting
probabilities of $r$ over every finite initial interval of times is at most $B$, then
for every positive natural number $t$, the probability that $r$ has not halted on a
uniformly random length-$t$ bit string is at most $B/t$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[A Small Nonhalting Probability]
\lean{Randomized.exists_notHaltedProb_le}
\label{Randomized.exists_notHaltedProb_le}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.ExpTimeLe, Randomized.ExpTimeLe.nonneg, Randomized.IsPrefixStable, Randomized.notHaltedProb, Randomized.notHaltedProb_le_div}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\alpha$ be a type, and let $r$ map bit strings to either an element of $\alpha$ or
no value. Suppose that whenever $r(w)$ has a value, appending any bit string to $w$
leaves that value unchanged. Assume there is a rational bound $B$ such that for every
nonnegative integer $K$, the sum, over $0\le t<K$, of the probability that $r$ has no
value on a uniformly random $t$-bit string is at most $B$. Then for every rational
$\varepsilon>0$, some nonnegative integer $t$ has probability at most $\varepsilon$ that
$r$ has no value on a uniformly random $t$-bit string.
\end{theorem}

Let $r$ be a function from finite Boolean words to either an output in a set $\alpha$ or

Let $r$ be a function from finite Boolean words to either an output in a set $\alpha$ or

\begin{theorem}[Expected Time Bound from Eventual Halting]
\lean{Randomized.expTimeLe_of_forall_ne_none}
\label{Randomized.expTimeLe_of_forall_ne_none}

\begin{theorem}[Nonhalting probability under repeated runs]
\lean{Randomized.notHaltedProb_repeatRun}
\label{Randomized.notHaltedProb_repeatRun}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.notHaltedProb, Randomized.randProb, Randomized.randProb_congr, Randomized.randProb_split, Randomized.randProb_true, Randomized.repeatRun, Randomized.repeatRun_of_le, Randomized.repeatRun_of_lt}
\difficulty{4}
Let $q$ be a procedure that returns either an output or no output on a finite bit
string, and let $t,m$ be natural numbers with $0<t$. For any natural number $s<t$,
consider the procedure that repeatedly runs $q$ on successive blocks of $t$ bits,
stopping at the first output and returning no output if no such output occurs. On a
uniformly random string of $mt+s$ bits, its probability of returning no output equals
the $m$th power of the probability that $q$ returns no output on a uniformly random
string of $t$ bits.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Expected runtime of repeated runs]
\lean{Randomized.expTimeLe_repeatRun}
\label{Randomized.expTimeLe_repeatRun}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.ExpTimeLe, Randomized.notHaltedProb, Randomized.notHaltedProb_nonneg, Randomized.notHaltedProb_repeatRun, Randomized.randProb, Randomized.randProb_nonneg, Randomized.repeatRun}
\difficulty{5}
Let $t$ be a positive integer and let $q$ be a randomized procedure that, on a string of
$t$ bits, either returns an output or does not halt. Suppose a uniformly random $t$-bit
string makes $q$ fail to halt with probability at most $1/2$. Run $q$ repeatedly on
successive blocks of $t$ bits, stopping at the first block on which it returns an
output; the sum, over every finite cutoff $K$, of the probabilities that this procedure
has not halted after $s$ bits for each $0 \le s < K$ is at most $2t$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Halting run output]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.haltRun}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.haltRun}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.outputWith, Turing.NDTM.initCfg, Turing.NDTM.runWith}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input and output, and
let $x$ and $w$ be finite Boolean strings. The halting-run output is the machine's
output on input $x$ along choice string $w$ if that run has halted, and is undefined
otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Bounded expected halting time]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.ExpTimeLe}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.ExpTimeLe}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.ExpTimeLe, Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.haltRun}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input and output, let
$x$ be a finite Boolean string, and let $B$ be rational. The machine's cumulative
probability of not having halted, summed over all times $t<K$, is at most $B$ for every
natural number $K$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Characterizing a specified halting output]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.haltRun_eq_some_iff}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.haltRun_eq_some_iff}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM.haltRun, Turing.FinNDTM.outputWith, Turing.NDTM.initCfg, Turing.NDTM.runWith}
\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input and output, and
let $x,w,o$ be Boolean words. The halting-run result on input $x$ under choices $w$
equals the output word $o$ if and only if the machine is in its halting state after
those choices and its output word is $o$.
\end{theorem}

let $x$ and $w$ be Boolean words. The halting-run result on input $x$ under choices $w$
is absent if and only if the machine’s state after those choices is not the halting
state.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Zero-error decision within time bound]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.ZDecidesInTime}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.ZDecidesInTime}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.ExpTimeLe, Turing.FinNDTM.outputWith, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator, Turing.NDTM.initCfg, Turing.NDTM.runWith}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input and output, let
$L$ be a language of finite Boolean strings, and let $T$ assign a natural-number time
bound to each natural number. For every input string $x$, the cumulative probability of
not having halted, summed over all times, is at most the time bound $T(|x|)$; moreover,
every choice string whose run halts produces the one-symbol output indicating whether
$x$ belongs to $L$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Abort decision within time bound]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.AbortDecidesInTime}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.AbortDecidesInTime}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.outputProb, Turing.FinNDTM.outputWith, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator, Turing.NDTM.HaltsWithin}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input and output, let
$L$ be a language of finite Boolean strings, and let $T$ assign a natural-number time
bound to each natural number. For every input string $x$, every run halts within
$T(|x|)$ steps; every choice string of length exactly $T(|x|)$ produces an output
different from the one-symbol answer indicating whether $x$ belongs to $L$; and the
probability that the output after $T(|x|)$ steps is that one-symbol answer is at least
$1/2$.
\end{definition}

Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over Boolean symbols, let $L$ be a
language of Boolean words, and let $T\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that $N$

\end{theorem}

language of Boolean words, and let $T\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that on
every input $x$, the sum over all time horizons of the probabilities that the run of $N$
has not halted is at most $T(|x|)$, and every run that halts outputs the one-symbol word
indicating whether $x\in L$. Then, for every input $x$, every halting run outputs that
correct one-symbol word, and a uniformly chosen Boolean choice word of length $2T(|x|)$
yields a halting run with that output with probability at least $1/2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Halting output under output flipping]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.haltRun_flipOutput}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.haltRun_flipOutput}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM.flipOutput, Turing.FinNDTM.flipOutput_outputWith, Turing.FinNDTM.haltRun, Turing.NDTM.flipOutput, Turing.NDTM.flipOutput_initCfg, Turing.NDTM.flipOutput_runWith, Turing.NDTM.initCfg, Turing.NDTM.runWith}
\difficulty{3}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input and output, and
let $x$ and $w$ be Boolean words. The halting-run result for the machine obtained by
flipping $N$’s output on input $x$ under choices $w$ is the result for $N$ on the same
input and choices with each output bit negated, leaving an absent result absent.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Complementation by flipping output]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.ZDecidesInTime.flipOutput}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.ZDecidesInTime.flipOutput}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.notHaltedProb, Randomized.randProb_congr, Turing.FinNDTM.ZDecidesInTime, Turing.FinNDTM.flipOutput, Turing.FinNDTM.haltRun, Turing.FinNDTM.haltRun_eq_some_iff, Turing.FinNDTM.haltRun_flipOutput, Turing.FinNDTM.outputWith, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator}
\difficulty{5}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over Boolean symbols, let $L$ be a
language of Boolean words, and let $T\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. If $N$ has total
nonhalting probability at most $T(|x|)$ on every input $x$, and every run that halts
outputs the one-symbol indicator of whether $x\in L$, then the machine obtained by
complementing each output bit has total nonhalting probability at most $T(|x|)$ on every
input and outputs the one-symbol indicator of whether $x\notin L$ on every halted run.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Correctness and expected time of restart]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.AbortDecidesInTime.restart}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.AbortDecidesInTime.restart}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.ExpTimeLe, Randomized.exists_of_repeatRun_eq_some, Randomized.expTimeLe_repeatRun, Randomized.randProb, Randomized.randProb_mono, Randomized.randProb_not, Randomized.repeatRun, Turing.Cfg.init, Turing.FinNDTM.AbortDecidesInTime, Turing.FinNDTM.bitOfOutput, Turing.FinNDTM.outputProb, Turing.FinNDTM.outputWith, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator, Turing.NDTM.initCfg}
\difficulty{5}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, $L$ a
language of binary strings, and $T$ a natural-number-valued time bound, and suppose $N$
satisfies the aborting decision conditions with time bound $T$. Fix a binary input $x$.
Consider the procedure that repeatedly runs $N$ on $x$ in blocks of $T(|x|)$ choices,
returning the bit if a block's output is exactly a one-bit string and otherwise
continuing. Its expected number of choices, expressed as the sum of its probabilities of
not having returned a result through each finite horizon, is at most $2T(|x|)$;
moreover, whenever it returns a bit, that bit equals the indicator of whether $x\in L$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Zero-error time complexity class]
\lean{Randomized.ZTIME}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch07-randomized-computation}{pdf-26d95080dbde-p007-b001}
\label{Randomized.ZTIME}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.ZDecidesInTime}
For a function $T:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$, let $\mathrm{ZTIME}(T)$ be the class of
languages over the Boolean alphabet that are decided by some nondeterministic Turing
machine within time $cT(n)$ on inputs of length $n$, for some natural-number constant
$c$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Zero-error polynomial time class]
\lean{Randomized.ZPP_PTM}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch07-randomized-computation}{pdf-26d95080dbde-p007-b001}
\label{Randomized.ZPP_PTM}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.ZTIME}
The class $\mathrm{ZPP}$ is the union, over all natural numbers $c$, of the classes of
Boolean languages decidable by a nondeterministic Turing machine in time $c(n^c+1)$ on
inputs of length $n$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Polynomial-time abort-decision class]
\lean{Randomized.ZPPAbort_PTM}
\label{Randomized.ZPPAbort_PTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.AbortDecidesInTime}
The class is the union, over all natural numbers $c$, of the languages $L$ over the
Boolean alphabet for which there exist a natural number $a$ and a finite
nondeterministic Turing machine that abort-decides membership in $L$ within time
$a(n^c+1)$ on inputs of length $n$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of zero-error time]
\lean{Randomized.ZTIME.mono}
\label{Randomized.ZTIME.mono}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.ZTIME}
\difficulty{2}
Let $T_1,T_2:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ satisfy $T_1(n)\le T_2(n)$ for every $n$. Then
every language decidable in zero-error expected time bounded by $T_1$ is also decidable
in zero-error expected time bounded by $T_2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Complement closure of randomized time classes]
\lean{Randomized.compl_mem_ZTIME}
\label{Randomized.compl_mem_ZTIME}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.ZTIME, Turing.FinNDTM.ZDecidesInTime.flipOutput, Turing.FinNDTM.flipOutput}
\difficulty{1}
For every function $T:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ and every language $L$ of Boolean
strings, if $L$ belongs to $\mathrm{ZTIME}(T)$, then its complement also belongs to

\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial time is contained in ZPP]
\lean{Randomized.P_subset_ZPP_PTM}
\label{Randomized.P_subset_ZPP_PTM}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.P, Randomized.DTIME_subset_ZTIME, Randomized.ZPP_PTM}
\difficulty{1}
Every language decidable by a finite deterministic Turing machine in polynomial time
belongs to the class of languages decided by a finite randomized Turing machine with
zero error and polynomial expected running time, where the expected-time bound is
expressed by a uniform bound on the sum, over every finite time horizon, of the
probabilities that the machine has not halted by each time.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Restarting a zero-error randomized verifier]
\lean{Randomized.InZPP.restart}
\label{Randomized.InZPP.restart}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.ExpTimeLe, Randomized.InZPP, Randomized.VerifierModel, Randomized.exists_ofFn_eq, Randomized.exists_of_repeatRun_eq_some, Randomized.expTimeLe_repeatRun, Randomized.polyLen, Randomized.randProb, Randomized.randProb_take, Randomized.repeatRun}
\difficulty{5}
Let $E$ be a verifier model and $L$ a language of bit strings. If $L$ has a zero-error
randomized verifier that runs efficiently, uses polynomially many random bits, never
rejects a member, never accepts a nonmember, and halts with probability at least $1/2$
on each input, then there are an efficient verifier $M$ and natural numbers $a,k$ such
that, on each input $x$, restarting runs of $M$ on fresh blocks of $|x|$-dependent
random bits yields a procedure whose sum of nonhalting probabilities over its first $K$
time bounds is at most $2(N+1)$ for every natural number $K$, where $N=a(|x|+1)^k$.
Moreover, whenever this restarted procedure returns a Boolean value on any bit string of
random bits, that value is true exactly when $x\in L$. Each run uses blocks of $N+1$
bits, and the repeated-run procedure returns the first nonhalting result within the
available blocks.
\end{theorem}
